label: FRITZ!Powerline 1220E powerline adapter
description: HomePlug AV2 1200 adapter, 2x GbE RJ45, integrated 230 V socket with line filter.
notes: AVM specs: 2 x gigabit LAN RJ45, up to 1200 Mbit/s HomePlug AV2, 128-bit AES, IGMP, ~1 W standby, 59 x 132 x 41 mm. Backwards compatible with 1200/500/200 Mbit/s and IEEE P1901.

label: FRITZ!Powerline 1260E powerline + Wi-Fi adapter
description: HomePlug AV2 1200 adapter, 1x GbE, Wi-Fi AC 866 (5 GHz) + N 400 (2.4 GHz) concurrent.
notes: AVM specs: 1 x gigabit LAN, up to 1200 Mbit/s HomePlug AV2, Wireless AC up to 866 Mbit/s gross on 5 GHz and N up to 400 Mbit/s gross on 2.4 GHz with concurrent dual-band, WPS button, FRITZ!OS web UI.

label: ScreenBeam ECB6250 MoCA 2.5 adapter (1G Ethernet)
description: MoCA 2.5 bridge: 1x 1G RJ45 + coax, up to 2.5 Gbps on the coax.
notes: ScreenBeam page: 'MoCA 2.5 Network Adapter with 1.0Gbps Ethernet Port'; up to 2.5 Gbps MoCA throughput, 1 Gbps at the Ethernet port; 16 nodes; MPS pairing; backward compatible with MoCA 2.0/1.1/1.0. Sits between the ECB6200 (bonded MoCA 2.0, 1G) and the ECB7250 (2.5GbE) already in the catalogue.

label: FRITZ!Powerline 1240E (NOT CATALOGUED)
notes: OPEN: AVM's technical-specifications URL for the 1240E returns 404 on the current site (the product appears to have been retired from the line-up), so its port count could not be confirmed from the vendor. Left out rather than inferred from the 1220E/1260E pattern.

label: Comtrend PG-9172 G.hn powerline adapter (NOT CATALOGUED)
description: G.hn 1200 powerline adapter with pass-through variants (PG-9172PT, PG-9172PoE).
notes: RESOLVED: datasheet DS_PG-9172_V1.0.3 read - 1x RJ-45 10/100/1000BaseT, G.hn PHY up to 1200 Mbps, 802.1D bridge, 802.1Q VLAN, IGMP/MLD snooping, AES-128, TR-069, 16 nodes, HomeGrid certified. Catalogued as comtrend/pg-9172.json with the mains port at 1G (ladder has no 1200 rung). It is the catalogue first G.hn mains part and does not interoperate with the HomePlug parts.

label: PLP2000 - pre-existing rate overstatement, flagged not fixed
description: NETGEAR Powerline 2000 + Extra Outlet, already in the catalogue declaring plc0 at 2.5G.
notes: FINDING while adding the AVM parts: PLP2000's plc0 is declared at 2.5G, which puts it on the engine's ghn-25 rung - but the PLP2000 is a HomePlug AV2 adapter whose '2000' is a 2000 Mbit/s PHY rate, not a 2.5GBASE-T-class mains link, and HomePlug AV2 tops out on the engine's homeplug-av2 medium (1000 Mbps). The AVM parts hit the same wall from the other side: their honest 1200 Mbit/s is not on the ladder at all (200/1000/1700/2500), so they are declared at 1G. Suggested follow-up: either add a 1200 rung to CAGE_SPEEDS.powerline (engine/optical-adjacent table in engine/media.js) or correct PLP2000 down to 1G. Left alone here because it changes an existing device's modelled capability and belongs in its own commit with the ladder decision.

label: G.hn2400 Powerline AX1800 Wi-Fi 6 kit (NOT CATALOGUED)
description: G.hn 2400 extender (PGW2440) + passthrough adapter (PG2400P), Wi-Fi 6 AX1800.
notes: OPEN + why: TP-Link states G.hn2400 rate and AX1800 Wi-Fi 6, but the kit page does not give the per-unit LAN port count for the PGW2440 (the PG2400P adapter is already in the catalogue), and 2400 Mbit/s is not on the engine powerline ladder either. Needs the PGW2440 datasheet and the ladder fix (add 1200 and 2400 rungs) before it can be added honestly. Note also: TP-Link state the G.hn kits are NOT compatible with HomePlug AV/AV2 - a real lab constraint worth modelling once both families are present.
